name: Shephatiah
overview: Shephatiah was a male member of the tribe of Simeon who served as a chief officer for the Simeonites. He is specifically identified as the son of Maacah in the biblical record. His role as a leader among the Simeonites highlights his position of authority within his tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Shephatiah means 'y-h-v-h has judged.' It is a proper name recorded in Scripture but was not given directly by God. This meaning reflects a recognition of divine judgment associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Shephatiah is explicitly recorded as the son of Maacah. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further details about his family relationships apart from what is noted in his unique attribute.
scriptureSignificance: Shephatiah's significance lies in his leadership role as a chief officer for the Simeonites, indicating his responsibility in the organization and governance of his tribe. His mention in Scripture, though brief, preserves his place among the leaders appointed during the reign of King David. This underscores the orderly structure God established within Israel's tribes through appointed leaders.
